headline: Future Consumer Limited: Appointment of Resolution Professional in Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: Future Consumer Limited has initiated formal Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 with the appointment of a resolution professional. The intimation was filed with NSE, triggering statutory disclosure obligations and triggering the 180-day (extendable) resolution window under IBC.
implication: The RP appointment marks entry into formal CIRP; creditors must now lodge claims within the prescribed timeline, and the estate is ring-fenced from operational creditor harassment - a critical gating point for restructuring or liquidation outcomes in retail-sector insolvencies.
detail: Future Consumer Limited, a major player in the modern retail and FMCG distribution segment, has formally entered CIRP following an order by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) or acknowledgement by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI). The appointment of a resolution professional is the mandatory first step in the statutory 180-day CIRP window, during which a Committee of Creditors (CoC) will be constituted and creditor claims admitted. The company will be under moratorium, halting all enforcement proceedings. The resolution professional will prepare an Information Memorandum (IM) and invite resolution plans from eligible bidders (financial entities, operational creditors, group companies subject to eligibility rules). The outcome will be either a successful resolution plan approved by CoC, or liquidation under IBC Schedule II.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, §5 (corporate debtor definition), §10 (CIRP initiation), §16 (appointment of RP)
framework.note: central: defines the CIRP process, RP roles, and statutory timeline.

framework.ref: IBC 2016, §14 (IBBI as regulator), IBBI Regulations 2016 (CIRP), §27 (constitution of CoC), §30 (approval of resolution plan)
framework.note: central: procedural framework for CoC formation, creditor admission, and plan approval.
central: all enforcement actions freeze; operational creditors cannot pursue recovery during CIRP.

framework.ref: IBC 2016, §25 (resolution plan eligibility), §29A (resolution plan competition rules)
framework.note: amended: Section 29A was substantially amended in 2018 and 2020; current rules bar promoters of insolvent corporates for 3–5 years unless specifically approved by CoC.

framework.ref: IBBI (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) Regulations, 2016, Reg 36 (Information Memorandum), Reg 37 (request for resolution plans)
framework.note: central: governs IM preparation and bidding process rules.

framework.ref: NCLT (National Company Law Tribunal) Rules, 2016, Part II, Chapter IV (CIRP procedures)
framework.note: procedural: NCLT bench rules for hearings, interim relief, and order confirmation.

framework.ref: Secretarial Standards on Insolvency (issued by Institute of Company Secretaries of India)
framework.note: non-mandatory guidance; best practice for documentation and CoC proceedings.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Listing Regulations, 2015, Reg 30 (material event disclosure), Reg 47 (website disclosures)
framework.note: central: Future Consumer is likely listed; stock exchange filing obligations apply throughout CIRP.
fallback: if resolution fails, assets are sold and proceeds distributed per statutory waterfall.

conditions: Admission of creditor claims within prescribed timeline (typically 14 days from RP appointment notice)
Constitution of Committee of Creditors with voting rights weighted by debt amount
Approval of Information Memorandum by CoC
Receipt and evaluation of resolution plans from eligible bidders
CoC approval of a resolution plan by 66% voting share threshold (or 90% if promoter is bidder)
NCLT confirmation of approved plan (or liquidation if no plan approved)
Moratorium on all enforcement proceedings throughout CIRP
approvals: NCLT order admitting CIRP petition (or IBBI acknowledgement if initiated by creditor petition)
IBBI oversight of RP conduct and process
CoC approval of RP actions and resolution plan
NCLT final confirmation of resolution plan or liquidation order
Stock exchange continuous disclosure compliance (NSE/BSE intimations)
structure.novel: No structural novelty apparent; this is a standard CIRP entry for a retail/FMCG distribution company under the statutory 180-day framework.

triggers.note: creditor or company must satisfy default threshold (typically ₹1 lakh+ for operational creditors, any amount for financial creditors); NCLT admission is the gate.

triggers.law: SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015, Reg 30 and MCA-supervised entity disclosures
triggers.note: listed entity must immediately intimated stock exchange of CIRP initiation; NSE/BSE publish on disclosure platform.

triggers.law: IBBI Regulations, 2016, Reg 5–10 (RP eligibility and appointment)
triggers.note: IBBI-registered professional must be appointed; conflict-of-interest checks apply.
promoters, related parties, and persons disqualified under §29A cannot submit plans unless expressly permitted by CoC; critical gating for restructuring vs. sale.
